typography.serifUsedFor: mastheads, section heads, and large numerals ONLY

shadows.note: hairline borders and translucency carry elevation; drop shadows are reserved for the ⌘K bar and modals

motion.pageTransition: 620ms horizontal camera move, then cards settle on staggered delays

preferredPrimitives: HqShell (src/components/hqShell.tsx) — sidebar, island bar, room background, ⌘K
ScaleMarks (src/components/scaleMarks.tsx) — dots on a scale with a marked line
patterns: .dk-sec — section head with a right-hand key
.rs-plate .dk-table — translucent plate wrapping a dense table
DeckFocusProvider + focusBinding + useDeckKeys (src/components/deckFocus.tsx) — one person lit across the tiles, the marks and the table; arrow keys walk the roster, p holds a person
ScaleMarks (src/components/scaleMarks.tsx) — the shared lead-tile instrument on all three pages
Num (src/components/deckFocus.tsx) — a figure that travels to its new value when the window changes
useFlip (src/lib/deckMotion.ts) — rows move to their new place on a sort

must: Use CSS custom properties from truHqDark.css. Never hardcode a hex or rgba that a token already covers.
Every surface is translucent so the background render shows through. --lift for a surface sitting ON a card; never --panel or --base for an inner surface.
Amber (--accent) is scarce on purpose. Colour ONLY the one thing that needs action. If everything is amber, nothing reads as urgent.
Sea green = good, amber = needs attention, ember = bad, --text-40 = no data. Never repurpose these.
Animate transform and opacity only. Never animate top/left/width/height.
Staggered entrances use animation-fill-mode: backwards, NEVER both — `both` makes opacity 0 the resting state and a stalled animation leaves a blank page.
A wrapper that keeps a transform becomes the containing block for position:fixed descendants. Page-level animations must end at transform: none.
Every clickable element must be reachable by keyboard: a real button, or role + tabIndex + Enter/Space. Modals close on Escape.
Every number on screen must trace to a real loader. No invented data, no placeholder copy.
avoid: Tailwind, shadcn, Radix, styled-components — this project is hand-written CSS and pasting them is not portable.
<filter> / feGaussianBlur inside a full-viewport SVG background — it rasterises at display resolution and freezes the renderer. Bake softness into gradient stops.
backdrop-filter on cards — costs a compositing layer per card per scroll frame for almost no visual gain here.
Opaque cards. They were why the depth never landed.
Drawn hairline artwork crushed into a small card — it reads as scribbles.
Decorative dividers and wave SVGs between sections.
Type selectors in a class rule (.tru-room i) that silently outrank a class-only rule (.tru-room-core) — this caused a live rendering bug.
Large bold sans headings inside panels — the masthead is the only large type on a page.

decisions.choice: Forest palette: deep green ground, bone text, amber used sparingly for the single thing needing action.
decisions.why: Replaced the earlier warm-gold-on-near-black marketing palette for the app.

decisions.choice: One page transition owns arrival: a 620ms horizontal camera move, then cards settling on staggered delays from a single shared keyframe.
decisions.why: Three uncoordinated entrance systems (setTimeout reveals, per-row CSS stagger, room flare) were racing and read as stutter.

decisions.choice: One layout whether or not an agent sheet is open; the way back lives in the island bar.
decisions.why: Opening an agent used to drop dk-main and restore the retired top bar, so the sheet looked like an older product.

decisions.choice: All three deck pages carry the SAME lead-tile instrument — ScaleMarks — on three different axes: a rate (Pulse), elapsed days (Coach), position in a sequence (Rep).
decisions.why: Coach and Rep were showing captions that described pictures ('rings are 7, 14 and 30 days', 'every dot is an agent, every mark a module') over empty cards. The canvas artwork those sentences belonged to was cut for reading as scribbles at card size, and the words outlived it. One instrument beats three chart types.

decisions.choice: The tiles and the table are one instrument: pointing at a person anywhere lights them everywhere. Focus changes how much LIGHT a mark gets, never its colour.
decisions.why: A deck page drew the same team three times over with no wire between the copies — you could see that somebody was an outlier and had no way to find out who without reading every number. Changing colour on focus would have spent the amber that has to stay scarce.

decisions.choice: Dots that land on the same value stack upward rather than overlapping.
decisions.why: Three agents piled at module two is a fact about module two. Drawn flat it looked like one person and two missing ones, and it hid the difference between never-invited and stalled-at-zero.

decisions.choice: Sticky column headers on a deck table, but NOT a sticky totals row.
decisions.why: Pinned to the foot of the viewport the totals permanently covered whichever agent was at the bottom of the screen. Column names earn a strip of the screen; a second copy of the team average does not.
